CITY OF LANGFORD
MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF COUNCIL
Monday, April 6th, 2020 @ 5:30 p.m.
Due to COVID-19 Council Chambers is Closed
Public Dial-In Details will be posted at www.langford.ca
PRESENT
Remote by telephone: Mayor S. Young; Councillors: D. Blackwell, M. Sahlstrom, L. Seaton, N. Stewart, L.
Szpak, and R. Wade.
ATTENDING
In Person: Chief Administrative Officer, D. Kiedyk; Director of Corporate Services, B. Hutchins; Fire Chief, C.
Aubrey; Manager of Business Development and Events, D. Petrie; Manager of Information Technology, K.
Dube; Manager of Legislative Services, A. Proton; Manager of Community Safety and Municipal
Enforcement, L. Fletcher; and IT Systems Administrator, B. Agland.
Remote by telephone: Director of Finance, M. Dillabaugh; Director of Engineering, M. Mahovlich, Director
of Planning, M. Baldwin; and RCMP Officer in Charge, T. Preston.
1.
CALL TO ORDER
Mayor Young called the meeting to order at 5:32 pm.
APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA
2.
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR WADE
COUNCILLOR SEATON
SECONDED:
That Council approve the agenda with the addition of 8c) Bylaw No. 1907, 8d) Bylaw No. 1908, and
8e) Bylaw No. 1909.
CARRIED.
ADOPTION OF COUNCIL MINUTES

That Council approve the minutes of the regular meeting of Council held on March 16th, 2020;
the minutes of the special meeting of Council held on March 19th, 2020; and
the minutes of the special meeting of Council held on March 26th, 2020.
CARRIED.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
4.
Representative from West Shore Voice News - Requested more information about how a $10,000 fine in
proposed bylaw 1908 would be applied, and how many bylaw officers there are to enforce business
regulations. Staff clarified that the City can only ticket and initiate legal action, and that a fine up to $10,000
could only be laid by the courts. There are currently 3 Bylaw officers, plus the Manager of Community Safety
and Municipal Enforcement, and auxiliary officers.
NOTICE OF INTENT
5.
a) TUP20-0001 - 4373 West Shore Pkwy
MOVED BY: COUNCILLOR BLACKWELL
SECONDED: COUNCILLOR STEWART
That Temporary Use Permit No. TUP20-0001 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Ken
Demontigny of Galaxy Motors (0698721 BC Ltd.) to allow the land to be used for receiving, preparing and
storage of recreational vehicles for sale at the applicant's neighboring RV Dealership (4377 West Shore
Parkway) without building a structure that meets the 10% minimum lot coverage for lots with an area less
than 1,000 m subject to the following terms and conditions:
1. Conditions
The following requirements are imposed under Section 922 of the Local Government Act:
a) No razor wire fencing;
b) At least one 10lb dry chemical fire extinguisher must be available on site at all times;
c) Address for the site to be posted as per City of Langford bylaw; and
d) Maintain an access lane on site for fire suppression for the duration.
CARRIED.
6.
REPORTS
a) LLP20-0001 - Bear Mountain Liquor License, 1999 Country Club Way
Staff Report (Planning)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR SZPAK
COUNCILLOR SAHLSTROM
SECONDED:
That Council inform the Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch that the City of Langford will
 
Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting
April 6th, 2020
Page 3 of 6
opt out of the notification process for the Structural Change application for the existing Liquor
Primary License for the Bear Mountain Golf Club located at 1999 Country Club Way.
CARRIED.
b) Public Hearings
Staff Report (Planning)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR BLACKWELL
COUNCILLOR STEWART
SECONDED:
That Council direct staff to waive all Public Hearings for any zoning bylaws which receive 1s reading
on, or before, the World Health Organization rescinds the COVID-19 pandemic;
That Council pass the following resolution:
"Whereas Section 154(1)(a) and 155(2)(a1) of the Community Charter (SBC 2003) permits Council
as a whole to delegate its authority with respect to council hearings that are required by law or
authorized by enactment; and
Whereas a Public Hearing under Sec. 464 of the Local Government Act does not constitute a power
or duty established by an enactment that council hear an appeal or reconsider an action, decision
or other matter;
a) That Council delegate its authority to conduct a Public Hearing to Councillor Denise Blackwell in
those instances where a zoning amendment is to be considered in conjunction with an Official
Community Plan amendment; and
b) That Council delegate its authority to conduct a Public Hearing to Councillor Roger Wade in
those instances where a zoning amendment is to be considered in conjunction with an Official
Community Plan amendment and only when Councillor Denise Blackwell is unable to exercise
her delegated authority;
c) That this resolution be in effect until the World Health Organization rescinds the COVID-19
pandemic.
CARRIED.
c) Update on City of Langford COVID-19 Initiatives
- Staff Report (Administration)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR SAHLSTROM
COUNCILLOR SEATON
SECONDED:
That Council receive the update on the City of Langford COVID-19 Initiatives report

April 6*h, 2020

for information.
CARRIED.

a) BYLAW NO. 1898
"City of Langford Housing Agreement (948 Starling PI) Bylaw No. 1898, 2020".
(FIRST, SECOND AND THIRD READINGS)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR WADE
SECONDED: COUNCILLOR SAHLSTROM
That Council give Bylaw 1898 first, second and third readings.
CARRIED.
b) BYLAW NO. 1899
"Municipal Park Regulation Bylaw No. 177, Amendment No. 11, 2020"
(ADOPTION)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR WADE
SECONDED:
COUNCILLOR STEWART
That Council adopt Bylaw 1899.
CARRIED.
c) BYLAW NO. 1907
"Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993 Amendment Bylaw No. 1907, 2020."
(FIRST, SECOND, AND THIRD READINGS)
COUNCILLOR BLACKWELL
MOVED BY:
SECONDED:
COUNCILLOR SZPAK
That Council give Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993, Amendment Bylaw No. 1907, 2020 1st,
2nd, and 3rd reading; and
That Council direct staff to send Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993, Amendment Bylaw No.
1907, 2020 to the Provincial Minister of Health for deposit and to the Medical Health Officer for the
purposes of consultation with the expectation that the Medical Health Officer provide any
comments in writing by noon on April 20, 2020; and
That Council direct staff to provide an opportunity for those who may be affected by Ticket
Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993, Amendment Bylaw No. 1907, 2020 to provide submissions to the
City in writing by noon on April 20, 2020.
 
Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting
April 6th, 2020
Page 5 of 6
CARRIED.
d) BYLAW NO. 1908
"Business Regulation (COVID-19) Bylaw No. 1908".
(FIRST, SECOND AND THIRD READINGS)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR STEWART
COUNCILLOR SZPAK
SECONDED:
That Council give Business Regulation (Covid-19) Bylaw No. 1908, 2020, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd reading;
and
That Council direct staff to send Business Regulation (Covid-19) Bylaw No. 1908, 2020 to the
Provincial Minister of Health for deposit and to the Medical Health Officer for the purposes of
consultation with the expectation that the Medical Health Officer provide any comments in writing
by noon on April 20, 2020; and
That Council direct staff to provide an opportunity for those who may be affected by Business
Regulation (Covid-19) Bylaw No. 1908, 2020 to provide submissions to the City in writing by noon
on April 20, 2020.
CARRIED.
e) BYLAW NO. 1909
"Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993 Amendment Bylaw No. 1909, 2020."
(FIRST, SECOND, THIRD READINGS AND ADOPTION)
MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR BLACKWELL
SECONDED:
COUNCILLOR SZPAK
That Council give Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993, Amendment Bylaw No. 1909, 2020 1st,
2nd, and 3rd readings, and further that Council adopt Ticket Information Bylaw No. 34, 1993,
Amendment Bylaw No. 1909, 2020.
CARRIED.
9.

MOVED BY:
COUNCILLOR BLACKWELL
SECONDED:
COUNCILLOR SZPAK
THAT Council close the meeting to the public pursuant to section 90 (1) e and k of the
Community Ch1rter to consider:
the acquisition, disposition or expropriation of land or improvements, if the council

municipality; and
• negotiations and related discussions respecting the proposed provision of a municipal
service that are at their preliminary stages and that, in the view of the council, could
reasonably be expected to harm the interests of the municipality if they were held in
public.
CARRIED.
10.
ADJOURNMENT
Mayor Young adjourned the meeting at 6:00 pm.
CERTIFIED CORRECT
Corporate Officer

"Whereas Section 154(1)(a) and 155(2)(a1) of the Community Charter (SBC 2003) permits Council
as a whole to delegate its authority with respect to council hearings that are required by law or
authorized by enactment; and
Whereas a Public Hearing under Sec. 464 of the Local Government Act does not constitute a power
or duty established by an enactment that council hear an appeal or reconsider an action, decision
or other matter;
a) That Council delegate its authority to conduct a Public Hearing to Councillor Denise Blackwell in
those instances where a zoning amendment is to be considered in conjunction with an Official
Community Plan amendment; and
b) That Council delegate its authority to conduct a Public Hearing to Councillor Roger Wade in
those instances where a zoning amendment is to be considered in conjunction with an Official
Community Plan amendment and only when Councillor Denise Blackwell is unable to exercise
her delegated authority;
c) That this resolution be in effect until the World Health Organization rescinds the COVID-19
pandemic.
